1	//! UI theme (DESIGN.md §5.6, §5.12).
2	//!
3	//! Holds the customizable styling knobs the renderer reads each
4	//! frame. v1 ships a built-in default that matches vim's classic
5	//! split visuals (active status line reverse-videoed, inactive
6	//! dim, vertical separator with `│`); every field is exposed via
7	//! `:set ui.*` options so a user / config layer can override it.
8	//!
9	//! Adding a new themable surface is two edits: add a field to
10	//! [`Theme`] with its default + add an `OptionSpec` in
11	//! `crate::options::builtin_options()` that mutates that field.
12	
13	use ratatui::style::{Color, Modifier, Style};
14	
15	/// One full UI theme. Cheap to clone (Style + char fields are all
16	/// `Copy`); the App holds it directly and `:set ui.*` writes
17	/// through.
18	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
19	pub struct Theme {
20	    /// Per-pane status line style for the active pane. Default
21	    /// reverse-video + bold so focus is unambiguous regardless of
22	    /// the user's terminal palette.
23	    pub pane_status_active: Style,
24	    /// Per-pane status line style for inactive panes. Default
25	    /// dim + dark-gray foreground so the line is visible but
26	    /// clearly secondary.
27	    pub pane_status_inactive: Style,
28	    /// Style applied to every span in an inactive document pane
29	    /// when [`Self::dim_inactive_panes`] is true. Composes with
30	    /// the existing syntax-highlight style. Default: `DIM`
31	    /// modifier only -- preserves color, just reduces intensity.
32	    pub inactive_pane_overlay: Style,
33	    /// Whether inactive panes get [`Self::inactive_pane_overlay`]
34	    /// applied on top of their syntax highlights. Off → inactive
35	    /// panes look identical to active (just no terminal cursor).
36	    pub dim_inactive_panes: bool,
37	    /// Style for the vertical-split separator column (`│` between
38	    /// side-by-side panes). Default: dark gray foreground, no bg.
39	    pub pane_separator: Style,
40	    /// Character drawn in the vertical-split separator column.
41	    /// Default: `│` (U+2502, BOX DRAWINGS LIGHT VERTICAL).
42	    pub pane_separator_vertical: char,
43	    /// Character drawn in the horizontal-split separator row.
44	    /// Default: `─` (U+2500). Currently unused -- horizontal
45	    /// splits are visually delimited by the per-pane status line
46	    /// at the bottom of the upper pane. Reserved for layouts
47	    /// that disable per-pane status lines.
48	    pub pane_separator_horizontal: char,
49	
50	    // ---- Diagnostics (Phase 4.1.d.iii) ---------------------
51	
52	    /// Glyph + color for an Error-severity diagnostic. Rendered
53	    /// in the gutter's severity column; also drives the inline
54	    /// underline color when an error range overlaps text.
55	    pub diagnostic_error_glyph: char,
56	    pub diagnostic_error_style: Style,
57	    /// Warning severity.
58	    pub diagnostic_warning_glyph: char,
59	    pub diagnostic_warning_style: Style,
60	    /// Information severity.
61	    pub diagnostic_info_glyph: char,
62	    pub diagnostic_info_style: Style,
63	    /// Hint severity.
64	    pub diagnostic_hint_glyph: char,
65	    pub diagnostic_hint_style: Style,
66	}
67	
68	impl Default for Theme {
69	    fn default() -> Self {
70	        Self {
71	            pane_status_active: Style::new()
72	                .add_modifier(Modifier::REVERSED)
73	                .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
74	            pane_status_inactive: Style::new().fg(Color::DarkGray).add_modifier(Modifier::DIM),
75	            inactive_pane_overlay: Style::new().add_modifier(Modifier::DIM),
76	            dim_inactive_panes: true,
77	            pane_separator: Style::new().fg(Color::DarkGray),
78	            pane_separator_vertical: '│',
79	            pane_separator_horizontal: '─',
80	            // Severity glyphs: solid square / triangle / circle /
81	            // dot. Same shapes vim's nvim-lsp / VS Code use --
82	            // immediately readable, terminal-safe.
83	            diagnostic_error_glyph: '■',
84	            diagnostic_error_style: Style::new().fg(Color::Red).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
85	            diagnostic_warning_glyph: '▲',
86	            diagnostic_warning_style: Style::new()
87	                .fg(Color::Yellow)
88	                .add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD),
89	            diagnostic_info_glyph: '●',
90	            diagnostic_info_style: Style::new().fg(Color::Blue),
91	            diagnostic_hint_glyph: '·',
92	            diagnostic_hint_style: Style::new()
93	                .fg(Color::DarkGray)
94	                .add_modifier(Modifier::DIM),
95	        }
96	    }
97	}
98	
99	/// Resolve the per-severity rendering bits from the theme.
100	/// Returns `(glyph, style)`.
101	pub fn diagnostic_glyph_and_style(
102	    theme: &Theme,
103	    severity: lattice_lsp::DiagnosticSeverity,
104	) -> (char, Style) {
105	    match severity {
106	        lattice_lsp::DiagnosticSeverity::ERROR => {
107	            (theme.diagnostic_error_glyph, theme.diagnostic_error_style)
108	        }
109	        lattice_lsp::DiagnosticSeverity::WARNING => (
110	            theme.diagnostic_warning_glyph,
111	            theme.diagnostic_warning_style,
112	        ),
113	        lattice_lsp::DiagnosticSeverity::INFORMATION => {
114	            (theme.diagnostic_info_glyph, theme.diagnostic_info_style)
115	        }
116	        lattice_lsp::DiagnosticSeverity::HINT => {
117	            (theme.diagnostic_hint_glyph, theme.diagnostic_hint_style)
118	        }
119	        _ => (theme.diagnostic_info_glyph, theme.diagnostic_info_style),
120	    }
121	}
122	
123	/// Parse a user-typed color name into a ratatui [`Color`]. Accepts
124	/// the 16 ANSI names (lowercase + dark-prefixed variants) plus
125	/// `default` / `reset` for terminal-default. Hex colors arrive
126	/// post-1.0 (depends on a terminal-true-color check).
127	pub fn parse_color(s: &str) -> Result<Color, String> {
128	    Ok(match s.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
129	        "default" | "reset" => Color::Reset,
130	        "black" => Color::Black,
131	        "red" => Color::Red,
132	        "green" => Color::Green,
133	        "yellow" => Color::Yellow,
134	        "blue" => Color::Blue,
135	        "magenta" => Color::Magenta,
136	        "cyan" => Color::Cyan,
137	        "gray" | "grey" | "white" => Color::Gray,
138	        "darkgray" | "darkgrey" => Color::DarkGray,
139	        "lightred" => Color::LightRed,
140	        "lightgreen" => Color::LightGreen,
141	        "lightyellow" => Color::LightYellow,
142	        "lightblue" => Color::LightBlue,
143	        "lightmagenta" => Color::LightMagenta,
144	        "lightcyan" => Color::LightCyan,
145	        other => return Err(format!("unknown color `{other}`")),
146	    })
147	}
148	
149	#[cfg(test)]
150	mod tests {
151	    #![allow(clippy::unwrap_used)]
152	    use super::*;
153	
154	    #[test]
155	    fn default_theme_dims_inactive_panes() {
156	        let t = Theme::default();
157	        assert!(t.dim_inactive_panes);
158	    }
159	
160	    #[test]
161	    fn default_separator_is_box_drawing_vertical() {
162	        assert_eq!(Theme::default().pane_separator_vertical, '│');
163	    }
164	
165	    #[test]
166	    fn parse_color_named() {
167	        assert_eq!(parse_color("red").unwrap(), Color::Red);
168	        assert_eq!(parse_color("DarkGray").unwrap(), Color::DarkGray);
169	        assert_eq!(parse_color("default").unwrap(), Color::Reset);
170	    }
171	
172	    #[test]
173	    fn parse_color_unknown_errors() {
174	        assert!(parse_color("rainbow").is_err());
175	    }
176	}
